The rtk-wrapped `rtk git diff --stat` compact output preserved the same diffstat lines (sha256 differs only because of rtk's own formatting, not content loss for this small artifact -- content matched by eye and both files changed/inserted-line counts identical). An isolated RTK_DB_PATH ledger started at 0 total_commands and ended at 3 after the three rtk-wrapped invocations (compact + proxy-recovered + proxy-error), confirming the ledger tracked this second fixture correctly. avg_savings_pct was 0.0 for this small (44-byte) diffstat output -- rtk recorded no measurable compaction gain on an artifact this size, which is an honest negative/neutral result for the savings dimension even though exact-recovery and error-path preservation both held.

verdict_impact.explanation: RTK's proxy-exact-recovery and error-path-preservation properties, previously demonstrated on only the fixed six-commit git-log pair, now also hold on an independently constructed second repo and a different git subcommand, which broadens (but by only one additional pair) the use-stage evidence named in gap 6. limitations: Second pair uses a small (44-88 byte) diffstat artifact; rtk recorded 0.0 avg_savings_pct here, unlike the original six-commit git-log pair which showed nonzero compaction -- savings are artifact-size-dependent and this run does not establish a general savings claim.
